examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Expand a non-atomic read-modify-write into its read, computation and write steps. Preserve each thread's program order while exploring interleavings. A statement declared atomic in the problem must not be split. To establish a minimum/maximum, provide a realizing schedule and a bound excluding better outcomes.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Two threads each execute non-atomic x=x+1 once, initially x=0. What is the minimum final x under a sequentially consistent read/write model?

**Answer: 1.** Both can read 0 before either writes, then both store 1, losing one increment. At least one write occurs with a value at least 1, so the minimum is 1. Serial execution would give 2.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
This is an abstract concurrency model; a data race on ordinary variables in C/C++ can instead make program behaviour undefined.

Atomic loads and stores do not make a compound increment atomic.
